opus_eval.key_finding: Qwen 0.580 plan got highest non-ref Opus (22/40). Qwen 0.940 got only 17/40. Moderate correlation overall but poor in high-score region.

pairwise_test_cpr_prompt.accuracy: 50% (100% position bias, always picks first plan)
pairwise_test_cpr_prompt.verdict: UNUSABLE — original CPR prompt triggers extreme position bias in Qwen3-30B base model

pairwise_test_detailed_prompt.verdict: Qwen3-30B CAN discriminate plan quality with proper prompting. 85% at large gaps, 65% at small gaps.

dpo_implications.positive: Model has internal quality discrimination ability (85% at gap>=5). Position bias fixable via prompt design.
dpo_implications.concern_1: Small gap accuracy (65%) is moderate — DPO signal will be noisy for similar-quality pairs
dpo_implications.concern_2: In saturation zone (both Qwen>=0.7), pairwise accuracy drops to ~50% — DPO may not help break the ceiling
dpo_implications.concern_3: Qwen pairwise follows Qwen scalar preferences, NOT Opus. DPO with same-model preference = same Goodhart risk as RL with Qwen reward
dpo_implications.critical_insight: Using Qwen as BOTH policy AND preference model adds no new information. For DPO to beat RL, need an EXTERNAL preference signal (Opus, human, or stronger model).

experiments.exp_a_frozen_no_cr: Frozen model fresh mean = 0.416, NOT 0.047 as in v7-Frozen (seed difference). RL advantage over frozen baseline is much smaller than initially thought.
experiments.exp_b_rl_scores_only: RL+SO fresh=0.436 vs B4-SO fresh=0.409. Delta = +0.027. Within noise.
